answer_1.quote: We benchmark faithful calibration of LLMs through a comprehensive array of experiments spanning 19 models, 10 datasets, 6 content domains, and 5 uncertainty elicitation prompts...

answer_2.quote: We follow to compute dataset-level faithfulness as the conditional mean faithfulness generation (cMFG) score... We also score accuracy via LLM-as-a-Judge, computing Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier Score.

answer_3.quote: We use a LLM-as-a-Judge approach. Given a text input Q and response R, we first instruct an evaluator LLM to extract assertions... Another few-shot prompt is used to assess the decisiveness of each assertion.

answer_4.quote: We conducted a human annotation study... three expert annotators... We observed a high inter-annotator agreement of 0.89... annotators were asked to indicate which set of responses they found to communicate the model's confidence or uncertainty in a more helpful, reliable, and informative manner.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to judge which version better utilizes linguistic expressions of (un)certainty to convey its intrinsic (un)certainty in a helpful, informative, and reliable manner.
